goal.sl: Vprašaš Do you …? in Does she …? z glagolom v osnovni obliki, zanikaš z don't in doesn't, odgovoriš Yes, I do. No, she doesn't., vprašaš Where do you …? in veš, da be in have got ne potrebujeta do.
goal.de: Du fragst Do you …? und Does she …? mit dem Verb in der Grundform, verneinst mit don't und doesn't, antwortest Yes, I do. No, she doesn't., fragst Where do you …? und weißt, dass be und have got kein do brauchen.
goal.it: Chiedi Do you …? e Does she …? con il verbo alla forma base, dici di no con don't e doesn't, rispondi Yes, I do. No, she doesn't., chiedi Where do you …? e sai che be e have got non vogliono do.
goal.en: You can ask Do you …? and Does she …? with the verb in its base form, say no with don't and doesn't, answer Yes, I do. No, she doesn't., ask Where do you …?, and you know that be and have got take no do.

say.sl: Za vprašanje postavi **do** na začetek: **You live here.** (Živiš tu.) → **Do you live here?** (Ali živiš tu?) Pri **I**, **you**, **we** in **they** je to **do**, glagol pa ostane, kot je: **Do they walk to school?** (Ali hodijo v šolo peš?) Kratki odgovor ponovi **do**: **Yes, I do.** (Ja.)
say.de: Für die Frage kommt **do** nach vorn: **You live here.** (Du wohnst hier.) → **Do you live here?** (Wohnst du hier?) Bei **I**, **you**, **we** und **they** ist es **do**, und das Verb bleibt, wie es ist: **Do they walk to school?** (Gehen sie zu Fuß zur Schule?) Die Kurzantwort wiederholt **do**: **Yes, I do.** (Ja.)
say.it: Per chiedere, metti **do** davanti: **You live here.** (Abiti qui.) → **Do you live here?** (Abiti qui?) Con **I**, **you**, **we** e **they** è **do**, e il verbo resta com'è: **Do they walk to school?** (Vanno a scuola a piedi?) La risposta breve ripete **do**: **Yes, I do.** (Sì.)
say.en: To ask, put **do** in front: **You live here.** → **Do you live here?** With **I**, **you**, **we** and **they** it is **do**, and the verb stays as it is: **Do they walk to school?** The short answer takes **do** again: **Yes, I do.**

say.sl: Pri **he**, **she**, **it** in enem imenu je v vprašanju **does**: **Does Meg bark?** (Ali Meg laja?) **-s** gre k **does**, zato je glagol spet v osnovni obliki: **Meg barks.** → **Does Meg bark?** (nikoli *Does Meg barks?*) **Does Jack live on the fell?** (Ali Jack živi na hribu?) **Yes, he does.** (Ja.)
say.de: Bei **he**, **she**, **it** und einem Namen fragt man mit **does**: **Does Meg bark?** (Bellt Meg?) Das **-s** wandert zu **does**, das Verb steht wieder in der Grundform: **Meg barks.** → **Does Meg bark?** (nie *Does Meg barks?*) **Does Jack live on the fell?** (Wohnt Jack am Berg?) **Yes, he does.** (Ja.)
say.it: Con **he**, **she**, **it** e un nome la domanda vuole **does**: **Does Meg bark?** (Meg abbaia?) La **-s** passa a **does**, e il verbo torna alla forma base: **Meg barks.** → **Does Meg bark?** (mai *Does Meg barks?*) **Does Jack live on the fell?** (Jack abita sul monte?) **Yes, he does.** (Sì.)
say.en: With **he**, **she**, **it** or one name the question takes **does**: **Does Meg bark?** The **-s** goes to **does**, so the verb is back in its base form: **Meg barks.** → **Does Meg bark?** (never *Does Meg barks?*) **Does Jack live on the fell?** **Yes, he does.**

say.sl: Za zanikanje pride pred glagol **don't** (do not) ali **doesn't** (does not), glagol pa ostane v osnovni obliki: **I don't know.** (Ne vem.) **We don't live here.** (Ne živimo tu.) **Meg doesn't bark at night.** (Meg ponoči ne laja.), nikoli *doesn't barks*. Kratka odgovora: **No, I don't.** **No, she doesn't.** (Ne.)
say.de: Für nein kommt **don't** (do not) oder **doesn't** (does not) vor das Verb, und das Verb bleibt in der Grundform: **I don't know.** (Ich weiß es nicht.) **We don't live here.** (Wir wohnen nicht hier.) **Meg doesn't bark at night.** (Meg bellt nachts nicht.), nie *doesn't barks*. Die Kurzantworten: **No, I don't.** **No, she doesn't.** (Nein.)
say.it: Per dire di no, prima del verbo va **don't** (do not) o **doesn't** (does not), e il verbo resta alla forma base: **I don't know.** (Non lo so.) **We don't live here.** (Non abitiamo qui.) **Meg doesn't bark at night.** (Meg di notte non abbaia.), mai *doesn't barks*. Le risposte brevi: **No, I don't.** **No, she doesn't.** (No.)
say.en: For no, put **don't** (do not) or **doesn't** (does not) before the verb, which stays in its base form: **I don't know.** **We don't live here.** **Meg doesn't bark at night.** (never *Meg doesn't barks at night.*) The short answers: **No, I don't.** **No, she doesn't.**

say.sl: Vprašalnica, **where** (kje), **what** (kaj) ali **when** (kdaj), gre na začetek, za njo **do** ali **does**: **Where do you live?** (Kje živiš?) **What does Jack eat for breakfast?** (Kaj Jack je za zajtrk?) **When does the bus go?** (Kdaj gre avtobus?) V odgovoru je glagol kot vedno: **I live in Keswick.** (Živim v Keswicku.) **It goes in the morning.** (Gre zjutraj.)
say.de: Ein Fragewort, **where** (wo), **what** (was) oder **when** (wann), kommt zuerst, dann **do** oder **does**: **Where do you live?** (Wo wohnst du?) **What does Jack eat for breakfast?** (Was isst Jack zum Frühstück?) **When does the bus go?** (Wann fährt der Bus?) In der Antwort steht das Verb wie immer: **I live in Keswick.** (Ich wohne in Keswick.) **It goes in the morning.** (Er fährt am Morgen.)
say.it: Una parola interrogativa, **where** (dove), **what** (che cosa) o **when** (quando), va per prima, poi **do** o **does**: **Where do you live?** (Dove abiti?) **What does Jack eat for breakfast?** (Che cosa mangia Jack a colazione?) **When does the bus go?** (Quando parte l'autobus?) Nella risposta il verbo è come sempre: **I live in Keswick.** (Abito a Keswick.) **It goes in the morning.** (Parte la mattina.)
say.en: A question word, **where**, **what** or **when**, goes first, then **do** or **does**: **Where do you live?** **What does Jack eat for breakfast?** **When does the bus go?** The answer has the verb as usual: **I live in Keswick.** **It goes in the morning.**

say.sl: **be** in **have got** ne potrebujeta **do**: sama zamenjata mesto. **You're cold.** (Zebe te.) → **Are you cold?** (Te zebe?), nikoli *Do you are cold?* **Jack is at home.** (Jack je doma.) → **Is Jack at home?** **You've got a pen.** (Imaš pisalo.) → **Have you got a pen?** Sam **have** pa vzame **do**: tudi **Do you have a pen?** je prav.
say.de: **be** und **have got** brauchen kein **do**: Sie tauschen selbst den Platz. **You're cold.** (Dir ist kalt.) → **Are you cold?** (Ist dir kalt?), nie *Do you are cold?* **Jack is at home.** (Jack ist zu Hause.) → **Is Jack at home?** **You've got a pen.** (Du hast einen Stift.) → **Have you got a pen?** Aber **have** allein nimmt **do**: Auch **Do you have a pen?** ist richtig.
say.it: **be** e **have got** non vogliono **do**: cambiano posto da soli. **You're cold.** (Hai freddo.) → **Are you cold?** (Hai freddo?), mai *Do you are cold?* **Jack is at home.** (Jack è a casa.) → **Is Jack at home?** **You've got a pen.** (Hai una penna.) → **Have you got a pen?** Ma **have** da solo vuole **do**: anche **Do you have a pen?** è giusto.
say.en: **be** and **have got** take no **do**: they change places themselves. **You're cold.** → **Are you cold?** (never *Do you are cold?*) **Jack is at home.** → **Is Jack at home?** **You've got a pen.** → **Have you got a pen?** But **have** alone takes **do**: **Do you have a pen?** is right too.

translation.sl: Gospa Birkett vpraša pohodnika: — Ali hodite vsak dan po hribih? — Ne. Samo ob sobotah. — Ali hodi tudi vaša prijateljica? — Ja. Hodi do jezerca. — In kje živite? — V Penrithu, sem pa pridem na scone!
translation.de: Mrs Birkett fragt einen Wanderer: — Wandern Sie jeden Tag in den Bergen? — Nein. Nur samstags. — Wandert Ihre Freundin auch? — Ja. Sie wandert zum Bergsee. — Und wo wohnen Sie? — In Penrith, aber ich komme wegen der Scones hierher!
translation.it: Mrs Birkett chiede a un escursionista: — Cammina sui monti ogni giorno? — No. Solo il sabato. — Anche la sua amica cammina? — Sì. Va fino al laghetto. — E dove abita? — A Penrith, ma vengo qui per gli scones!
translation.en: Mrs Birkett asks a walker: — Do you walk on the fells every day? — No, I don't. Only on Saturdays. — Does your friend walk too? — Yes, she does. She walks to the tarn. — And where do you live? — In Penrith, but I come here for the scones!
